Hi Elaine — appreciate the clear asks and the questionnaire. Quick responses inline, plus a proposal for the short-term visibility request.

1) Uptime/availability: our hosted API measures availability as the percentage of successful request completions within a 1-minute window. Failures that count against availability are HTTP 5xx errors, gateway timeouts (30s+), and explicit internal service errors. Client-side cancellations (client closed connection) are excluded from uptime calculations.

2) Latency: we publish p50, p90, p95, and p99 for end-to-end request latency (request receive -> final token emitted). For model-level breakdowns (token gen time vs decoding vs I/O), we provide internal spans in the dashboard (these are the per-inference internal timings you can see in the Grafana traces). The p95 number you saw in the demo is end-to-end.

3) Alerting / Escalation: production SLO breaches trigger our incident pipeline: automated alerts to on-call (PagerDuty) for paging thresholds, and a 3-tier escalation (on-call -> platform lead -> SRE manager). Typical initial alerting threshold is a rolling 15-minute window exceeding the error budget by 20% (configurable per customer / plan). MTTR guidance: we commit to initial acknowledgment within 15 minutes for Dedicated customers; hosted customers have a 60-minute initial acknowledgment SLO.

4) Dashboard access / waiver: we can invite Atlas to a read-only Grafana view scoped to your org, but procurement understands account creation & legal steps can slow that. If you need something faster, we can issue a time-limited visibility waiver: a signed PDF that grants Atlas a 7-day scoped snapshot access (exported metrics + a single-use Grafana token). I'm happy to provide either immediately.

Attached a short runbook for the metrics definitions and a temp-invite text file we can publish if you choose the waiver route.

Would you like the 7-day waiver while procurement completes the account onboarding? If so, confirm an approval email from procurement and we will issue the token and the signed waiver.

Hi Elaine — quick technical clarifications from SRE/observability so procurement has precise answers for the questionnaire: 

- Uptime is derived from aggregated request outcomes at the edge layer aggregated per minute. "Success" is HTTP 2xx/3xx with response body; 429/4xx are counted separately (throttling) and do not count as outages unless they are systemic and correlated across regions.

- Error budget is calculated on a rolling 30-day window by default (we can change to 7/90-day per contract).

- Latency measurement: we measure from request ingress (load balancer receive) to final stream close. For streaming calls we report both first-byte and total-latency percentiles. We also surface model compute time (kernel execution & KV cache times) in the traces.

- Alerts: primary alert: sustained error rate above threshold for 15m -> PagerDuty page. Secondary: latency SLO breach for 30m -> on-call + platform lead. We publish post-incident RCA within 72 hours for incidents affecting >1% of customer requests.

- Customer metrics access: options:
  * Read-only Grafana invite (recommended) — scoped to SLO dashboards (no raw logs).
  * CSV metric export on request (we provide a signed CSV for procurement).
  * If neither is available immediately, we provide a signed waiver + 1-time token (7 days) that maps to a read-only single-dashboard view.

Retention: metrics retained at 1m granularity for 90 days; aggregated to 1h for 2 years for historical trending (per contract).

If procurement needs the exact query definitions we use for each SLO gauge, I can paste them or drop them into a shared doc.

Hi all — Jordan from Sales here. Thanks for the detailed thread. We can do the following to unblock procurement quickly:
